quote: There are things which are within our power, and there are things which are beyond our power.
author: Epictetus

quote: People are disturbed not by things, but by the views they take of them.
author: Epictetus

quote: Seek not that the things which happen should happen as you wish; but wish the things which happen to be as they are.
author: Epictetus

quote: No man is free who is not master of himself.
author: Epictetus

quote: Say to every harsh appearance: You are an appearance, and in no manner what you appear to be.
author: Epictetus

quote: When we are hindered or disturbed, let us never impute it to others, but to ourselves—that is, to our own views.
author: Epictetus

quote: Freedom is not procured by a full enjoyment of what is desired, but by controlling the desire.
author: Epictetus

quote: Remember that it is not he who reviles you or strikes you who insults you, but your opinion that these things are insulting.
author: Epictetus

quote: If you would improve, be content to be thought foolish and dull with regard to externals.
author: Epictetus

quote: If you hear that someone has spoken ill of you, do not make excuses about what was said, but answer: He does not know my other faults.
author: Epictetus

quote: Do not seek to appear a philosopher, but act according to your principles.
author: Epictetus

quote: Every habit and faculty is maintained and increased by the corresponding actions.
author: Epictetus

quote: First say to yourself what you would be; and then do what you have to do.
author: Epictetus

quote: Difficulties show what men are.
author: Epictetus

quote: It is in our power to make a right use of every event, and this no one can hinder.
author: Epictetus

quote: The happiness of your life depends upon the quality of your thoughts.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: You have power over your mind—not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: The soul becomes dyed with the color of its thoughts.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: If you are pained by any external thing, it is not this thing that disturbs you, but your own judgment about it.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Choose not to be harmed—and you will not feel harmed.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Our life is what our thoughts make it.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Nowhere can man find a quieter or more untroubled retreat than in his own soul.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Confine yourself to the present.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Reject your sense of injury and the injury itself disappears.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: The best revenge is not to be like your enemy.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Look well into yourself; there is a source of strength which will always spring up if you will always look.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: If it is not right, do not do it; if it is not true, do not say it.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Waste no more time arguing what a good man should be. Be one.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Have at hand thoughts brief and fundamental, sufficient to shut out the discordant clamour of the world.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: The mind, once withdrawn within itself, grows conscious of its own power.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
author: Seneca

quote: A man who suffers before it is necessary, suffers more than is necessary.
author: Seneca

quote: Most powerful is he who has himself in his own power.
author: Seneca

quote: The greatest remedy for anger is delay.
author: Seneca

quote: Anger, if not restrained, is frequently more hurtful to us than the injury that provokes it.
author: Seneca

quote: Begin at once to live, and count each separate day as a separate life.
author: Seneca

quote: If one does not know to which port one is sailing, no wind is favorable.
author: Seneca

quote: The mind should be allowed some relaxation, that it may return to its work all the better for the rest.
author: Seneca

quote: It does not matter what you bear, but how you bear it.
author: Seneca

quote: Associate with people who are likely to improve you.
author: Seneca

quote: No evil propensity of the human heart is so powerful that it may not be subdued by discipline.
author: Seneca

quote: Every night before sleep we must call ourselves to account.
author: Seneca

quote: All that we are is the result of what we have thought.
author: The Buddha

quote: If a man's thoughts are unsteady, if he does not know the true law, his knowledge will never be perfect.
author: The Buddha

quote: As rain does not break through a well-thatched house, passion will not break through a well-reflecting mind.
author: The Buddha

quote: Earnestness is the path of immortality; thoughtlessness is the path of death.
author: The Buddha

quote: One's own self is the master of oneself. Who else could be the master?
author: The Buddha

quote: By oneself evil is done; by oneself one suffers; by oneself evil is left undone.
author: The Buddha

quote: Let the wise man guard his thoughts, for they are difficult to perceive and very artful.
author: The Buddha

quote: A man should first direct himself in the way he should go; only then should he instruct others.
author: The Buddha

quote: He who controls his rising anger as a charioteer controls a rolling chariot, him I call a real driver.
author: The Buddha

quote: Not even a god can change into defeat the victory of a man who has vanquished himself.
author: The Buddha

quote: Knowing others is intelligence; knowing yourself is true wisdom.
author: Lao Tzu

quote: Mastering others is strength; mastering yourself is true power.
author: Lao Tzu

quote: He who knows that enough is enough will always have enough.
author: Lao Tzu

quote: To know that you do not know is the highest; not to know and yet think you know is a disease.
author: Lao Tzu

quote: He who conquers others is strong; he who conquers himself is mighty.
author: Lao Tzu

quote: Stillness is the master of unrest.
author: Lao Tzu

quote: Learning without thought is labour lost; thought without learning is perilous.
author: Confucius

quote: Real knowledge is to know the extent of one's ignorance.
author: Confucius

quote: When anger rises, think of the consequences.
author: Confucius

quote: When we see men of worth, we should think of equaling them; when we see men of a contrary character, we should turn inwards and examine ourselves.
author: Confucius

quote: The superior man is modest in his speech, but exceeds in his actions.
author: Confucius

quote: What the superior man seeks is in himself; what the small man seeks is in others.
author: Confucius

quote: The first and greatest victory is to conquer yourself.
author: Plato

quote: Opinion is the medium between knowledge and ignorance.
author: Plato

quote: Courage is knowing what not to fear.
author: Plato

quote: Knowledge which is acquired under compulsion obtains no hold on the mind.
author: Plato

quote: Thinking is the talking of the soul with itself.
author: Plato

quote: Anybody can become angry—that is easy; but to be angry with the right person, to the right degree, at the right time, for the right purpose, and in the right way—that is not easy.
author: Aristotle

quote: Happiness depends upon ourselves.
author: Aristotle

quote: The energy of the mind is the essence of life.
author: Aristotle

quote: It is the mark of an educated mind to be able to entertain a thought without accepting it.
author: Aristotle

quote: The greatest thing in the world is to know how to belong to oneself.
author: Michel de Montaigne

quote: He who fears he will suffer already suffers because he fears.
author: Michel de Montaigne

quote: Not being able to govern events, I govern myself.
author: Michel de Montaigne

quote: My art and profession is to live.
author: Michel de Montaigne

quote: I care not so much what I am to others as what I am to myself.
author: Michel de Montaigne

quote: It is not enough to have a good mind; the main thing is to use it well.
author: René Descartes

quote: I think, therefore I am.
author: René Descartes

quote: Conquer yourself rather than the world.
author: René Descartes

quote: Divide each difficulty into as many parts as is feasible and necessary to resolve it.
author: René Descartes

quote: An emotion which is a passion ceases to be a passion as soon as we form a clear and distinct idea of it.
author: Baruch Spinoza

quote: The highest activity a human being can attain is learning for understanding, because to understand is to be free.
author: Baruch Spinoza

quote: A free man thinks of death least of all things; and his wisdom is a meditation not of death but of life.
author: Baruch Spinoza

quote: The more we understand individual things, the more we understand the whole.
author: Baruch Spinoza

quote: All of humanity's problems stem from man's inability to sit quietly in a room alone.
author: Blaise Pascal

quote: The heart has its reasons, which reason does not know.
author: Blaise Pascal

quote: Man is but a reed, the most feeble thing in nature; but he is a thinking reed.
author: Blaise Pascal

quote: A man can do what he wills, but he cannot will what he wills.
author: Arthur Schopenhauer
source: On the Freedom of the Will

quote: Every man takes the limits of his own field of vision for the limits of the world.
author: Arthur Schopenhauer

quote: A man can be himself only so long as he is alone.
author: Arthur Schopenhauer

quote: The discovery of truth is prevented more effectively by preconceived opinion than by false appearances.
author: Arthur Schopenhauer

quote: Purity of heart is to will one thing.
author: Søren Kierkegaard

quote: Life can only be understood backwards; but it must be lived forwards.
author: Søren Kierkegaard

quote: Nothing can bring you peace but yourself.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: A man is what he thinks about all day long.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: It is not what you look at that matters, it is what you see.
author: Henry David Thoreau

quote: The mass of men lead lives of quiet desperation; what is called resignation is confirmed desperation.
author: Henry David Thoreau

quote: He who cannot obey himself will be commanded.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche
